what_its_for: This medicine helps prevent chest pain (angina) in people with heart disease. It works by relaxing and widening your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard. It is used regularly to prevent chest pain, not to treat chest pain that is already happening.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. If you take the extended-release tablet (Imdur), do not crush, chew, or break it. Take it at the same time each day to keep a steady level in your body. Follow your doctor's instructions carefully about timing, especially if you take more than one dose per day.
dosing: Your doctor will tell you the right dose for you. A common starting dose is 30 mg to 60 mg once daily in the morning for the extended-release tablet. For the regular tablet, it is often taken twice a day with doses 7 hours apart (for example, 8 AM and 3 PM). This gap is very important to prevent your body from getting used to the medicine too quickly. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in the original container with the cap tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine because it can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure, dizziness, or fainting. Do not take erectile dysfunction medicines such as sildenafil (Viagra), tadalafil (Cialis), or vardenafil (Levitra) while on this drug — this combination can cause a severe and life-threatening drop in blood pressure. Avoid standing up too quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine can make you feel dizzy. Be careful driving or using machinery until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe headache that does not go away, chest pain that is getting worse or is not being prevented by this medicine, fainting or severe dizziness, fast or irregular heartbeat, blurred vision, shortness of breath, or signs of a very low blood pressure such as feeling faint when you stand up. Seek emergency help immediately if you think you are having a heart attack.
when_it_works: This medicine starts to work within 30 to 60 minutes after you take it, but it is meant to be taken regularly to prevent chest pain over time. It is not fast-acting and should not be used to stop a chest pain episode that is already happening. If you get sudden chest pain, use a fast-acting nitrate like nitroglycerin spray or tablet as prescribed by your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution because you may be more sensitive to dizziness and low blood pressure. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. This medicine is not approved for use in children.
